newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo says weighing options after EU ruling.
newsitem.headline: Anglo says weighing options after EU ruling.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it was "very disappopinted" that the European Union had restricted its holding in Lonrho Plc but added it had various options to consider.

The European Commission, the EU's executive arm, said earlier that Anglo American had agreed to cut its stake in Lonrho to 9.99 percent from 27.5 percent in order to satisfy EU concerns about competition in the platinum market.
Anglo said it had been given two years to reduce its stake, leaving scope for an eventual satisfactory outcome.

Anglo said in a statement that the EU ruling placed an extreme construction on the definition of a decisive influence in a UK public company. It noted that it had stated from the outset that it had no intention of making a general offer for Lonrho.
Anglo's intention had been to build a relationship with Lonrho on a broad front, other than platinum.

"We had many hours of debate with the Commission and advanced many options accepted by other competition authorities including robust, legally binding ring-fencing undertakings," said Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson.
"We are, therefore, very disappointed by this ruling which has disturbing implications on the definition of decisive influence for the investment community.
"However, we have two years in which to divest this stake, a good relationship with Lonrho and a number of options to consider, so we are confident of a satisfactory outcome."

The Commission had expressed concern that Anglo's stake in Lonrho -- which has substantial interest in two South African platinum mines -- would put control of the world's platinum industry in the hands of Anglo and South African mining house Gencor Ltd.

It said its ruling maintained the strict application of European competition rules to the platinum sector, permitting the three South African platinum producers, Anglo, Lonrho and Gencor, to continue to exist separately.
